description: The Blockonauts are technology enthusiasts who enjoy learning, experimenting, and solving problems through innovation. For the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, we aim to make space and STEM learning fun and interactive. Our team brings experience in software development, APIs, cloud, AI, UI/UX, creative design, and problem-solving. We’re excited to combine technology, creativity, and storytelling to create a meaningful learning experience for young explorers.
summary:
COMMANDER is an interactive space-themed game developed by Team Blockonauts for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project is designed to make learning about space exploration more engaging by placing players in the role of a mission commander responsible for making important decisions during a space mission.
Through an immersive and interactive experience, COMMANDER combines space science, decision-making, problem-solving, and gaming to help users understand some of the challenges involved in space exploration. Players encounter mission-based scenarios where their choices influence progress and outcomes, encouraging them to think strategically while learning about space concepts.
The project transforms complex space-related ideas into an accessible and enjoyable digital experience, particularly for students and young space enthusiasts. By combining education with gamification, COMMANDER aims to spark curiosity about NASA missions, space technology, and STEM while demonstrating how interactive technology can make scientific learning more engaging and memorable.
details:
COMMANDER, developed by Team Blockonauts, is an interactive web-based space mission simulation created for the NASA Space Apps Hackathon. The project places users in the role of a mission commander, allowing them to make important decisions, manage challenges, and experience the responsibilities involved in a space mission. Through scenario-based gameplay, users learn how astronauts and mission-control teams respond to unexpected situations while balancing safety, resources, and mission objectives.

The project provides an engaging and accessible way to develop awareness of space exploration, teamwork, problem-solving, and decision-making. Its intended impact is to make space science more interesting for students and the general public by transforming complex mission concepts into an understandable, game-based experience. This aligns with the broader NASA Space Apps objective of using technology, creativity, and NASA-related data to address real-world challenges and encourage public participation in science and space exploration.

We developed the project using HTML, React, TypeScript, with Git and GitHub for source-code management and team collaboration, Vercel for Deployment.

The creativity of COMMANDER comes from combining education with interactive storytelling and mission-based gameplay. Instead of presenting space information as static text, the project allows users to learn through choices and consequences. While designing it, our team considered ease of use, visual appeal, scientific relevance, accessibility, performance, user engagement, and the limited development time of the hackathon. We also focused on making the experience understandable for users without an advanced scientific or technical background.

Project repository: NewNauts: NASA Space Apps Hackathon Submission Project
